comment: Declared allowances for knowledge decay, enforced by tests/checks/knowledge-drift.test.js against the generated supabase/knowledge-coverage.json. Same ratchet idiom as tests/reference-budget.json: each number is a CEILING, not a target, and a session that fixes rows lowers it in the same commit. The gates that came before this one check structure - that a vocabulary is documented, that a stored value renders, that the reference matches the code. This one checks CONTENT: whether what the system was told is still anchored, sourced and reachable. Four figures are already at 0 and are the interesting ones, because they are the promise being kept: every glossary term has a definition and a source, every journey stage has a source, every source document has a digest, and no finding claims a promotion with nothing behind it. Those must not rise. The rest are the honest backlog, and docs/HANDOVER-CONTEXT.md is the session that closes them.

notes.terms.no_definition: At 0 and must stay there. A term with no definition is a word in a list.
notes.terms.no_source: At 0 and must stay there. 35 terms, every one citing where it came from - owner-validated, a named document, a handover call, or PartnerPortal source. This is the figure that makes the glossary trustworthy rather than plausible.
notes.stages.no_source: At 0. All 13 cite the Merchant Portal Integration PRD and the date the owner validated them. Note that code-review wave 3 found the model and the code's 17 instrumented events disagree - see finding CR3-02 - which is a question about the model, not a missing source.
notes.documents.no_digest: At 0. docs/WORKFLOW.md requires raw material AND a digest; 18 of 18 have one. Rising means somebody pasted material and did not distil it, which is how a document becomes unsearchable.
notes.findings.promoted_without_item: At 0, and the schema constrains it too. Counted anyway because a constraint that is never exercised is a constraint nobody notices has been dropped.
notes.capabilities.no_area: 5 of 46. A capability with no area does not appear in the platform page's sections, so it is stored and effectively invisible. Lower this by filing them; they are not content the owner needs to supply.
notes.notes.orphaned: At 0, down from 20. Every note is anchored to an item or a document. Must not rise: an orphaned note is real content nothing links to.
notes.items.no_summary: 6 of 292, down from 80 of 268. A title alone is unreadable six months later, which is exactly when it gets read. Six left.
notes.items.closed_without_resolution: 40 of 292, and this is the one figure that DECAYED - it was 39 of 268, so the count rose while the ceiling stood. 'Nothing is ever deleted' means a closed row carries WHY it closed. One was recoverable on 2026-08-30: 'Refactoring and CLAUDE.md tidy-up' had its reason in details rather than resolution, and it was moved. The rest need the owner; some are recoverable from git or from notes.
notes.ideas.no_summary: At 0, down from 14 of 14. Every prototype idea now says what it is.
notes.ideas.no_value_note: At 0, down from 14 of 14. Every idea says what it would PROVE, which is the field that decides whether to build it.
notes.links.proposed: Raised 30 -> 41 on 2026-09-21. Only ONE is this session's: the relates_to recording that Contract Adjustments was carved out of Contract Management Features. Eleven others were written on 17 Sep and had gone unseen because supabase/knowledge-coverage.json had not been regenerated since 16 Sep - the staleness gate surfaced them, which is exactly what it is for. Still the one figure that rises when the system is used correctly, so the ratchet on it is a prompt to run a confirmation pass (docs/HANDOVER-CONTEXT.md section 4), not a defect count.
notes.embeddings.stale: At 0 and it must stay there. A vector computed from text that has since changed still answers searches, with the wrong meaning and no sign of it - the one failure here that actively misleads rather than merely missing. 33 were stale on 2026-08-30 and were cleared with select * from roadmap_embed_refresh(); it is idempotent, so running it when nothing is stale costs one query.
notes.items.no_benefit: Raised 79 -> 85 on 2026-09-15. Eleven rows were created by the Now restructure and five of them carry a drafted benefit; the other six are items whose benefit genuinely inherits from their workstream, which docs/VALUE-CAPTURE.md says is the normal case rather than a gap. The denominator rose too, from 166 to 177. Lower it by writing benefits for the rows that need their own, not by writing one on every child.
notes.items.benefit_unconfirmed: LOWERED 79 -> 65 on 2026-09-21, locking in a gain this session did not make: drafts were confirmed between 16 and 21 Sep and the artefact had not been regenerated to see it. One of the 65 IS this session's - the Contract Adjustments benefit, written by an assistant and drafted until the owner reads it. Only the owner can lower this further: confirmed means he has read that wording and agreed it, and an assistant may never set it, so this figure falls in a review session, never in a build one. Method: docs/VALUE-CAPTURE.md.
notes.items.no_association: Raised 60 -> 63 on 2026-09-21. Exactly three, and all three are the new Contract Adjustments items: PXP, DaoPay and per-MCC. Their parent workstream carries the product_technology association, and the playbook says not to repeat a parent's tag on every child, so they count here without being wrong - the same reason the 2026-09-15 rise was accepted. Raised 53 -> 60 on 2026-09-15 for the same shape of reason.
notes.areas.no_capability: 1 of 21, down from 8 in the 2026-09-07 grounding pass. The rule counts areas where work has SHIPPED and nothing describes it; an area with open items and nothing delivered has no capability to describe, and counting it would push a session to record intent as capability. The one left is Operations tooling & alerting, whose single closed row is a container its own resolution says was rehomed and parked rather than delivered - so it is arguably not a gap either, and a derivation record says so. Not forced to zero by writing a row for it.
notes.grounding.unattested: 4 of 46. Nobody has stood behind these either way. Lower it by attesting them - the owner accepting a row, or a session deriving it from rows the owner owns and linking the evidence.
notes.grounding.no_evidence: At 0 of 18 and must stay there. It is the promise the derived state rests on: a row marked derived that names no source is an assistant's assertion wearing the word derived. All 18 derived rows carry an about link to every delivered item behind them, and a derivation record naming the method and what was deliberately excluded.
notes.grounding.stale: 24 of 64, down from 38 of 46. The 18 derived rows carry the date of the newest source behind them, so they start current. The rest predate delivered work in their area and are the queue. This is the self-maintaining figure: shipping work marks the rows it may have invalidated, with nobody having to remember.
notes.grounding.delivered_without_affects: 65 of 83, RAISED from 35 of 35 - and the rise is progress, not decay. The denominator is delivered items in areas that HAVE capabilities, and the grounding pass gave seven more areas their first capability, so 48 delivered items entered the denominator that were not in it before. 18 affects links now exist where there were zero. Lower it by linking each delivered item to the capability it changed; ROADMAP-REVIEW Wave 4 is where that should happen without a sweep.
notes.endpoints.ungrounded: 133 of 572, down from all 572. Capabilities now claim the endpoints under the tags that serve them. What is left is mostly Unity payment surface - Point of Sale, Wallets, PayPal, Token Vault, Checkout, Smart Routing - plus Metrics and EIT management, none of which any capability describes. Will not reach zero and should not be forced there: a capability should claim the endpoints that serve it, not every endpoint that exists.
